newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL blue chips end down on thin trading.
newsitem.headline: KL blue chips end down on thin trading.

text.p: Malaysian blue-chip stocks closed lower on low volumes as fund managers stayed sidelined ahead of the requotation of several large-cap stocks, and the holiday in U.S. markets, analysts said.
"The market is waiting to see what happens on the relisting of Rashid Hussain, Maybank and the other banking stocks," said Simon Maughan, head of research at W.I. Carr.
The Composite Index of 100 large-capitalised stocks closed 4.58 points lower to 1,226.52, while the small-cap Second Board index ended down 1.39 points to 590.04.
Traded volume was the lowest of the week, said a dealer at a foreign brokerage research house in Kuala Lumpur.
At the close, 215 million shares had been traded, valued at 1,542 million ringgit. Losers pounded gainers by 349 to 206.
"It's the end of the month, and there may have been some futures-linked activity today," said the dealer.
Renong closed down 4.0 cents to 4.66 ringgit, while United Engineers ended down 40 to 22.90. Time Engineering was down 24 to 4.74.
The three firms declared results slightly below expectations on Thursday, analysts said.
